BiblicalUsage: Ararat is the mountain land where the ark rested when the waters went down, the land where Sennacherib's sons fled after murdering their father, and one of the kingdoms called to march against Babylon. The name runs from the flood to the fall of empires.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Ararat is where the old world ended and the new one began, because the ark came to rest there, and every story after it starts on dry ground.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
